title: How far off the carriers were
reading: 123 nm north of 107 at the tape's 03:14
basis: The tape's "123 DME on the 180" read as Nimitz's TACAN; that lands about 100 nm north of 32°30'N and about 190 nm off Sirte.

records.says: The carriers, Pentagon officials say, were well to the north, about 100 miles away from the gulf.
The two Navy Tomcats were stationed on the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier Nimitz, which was 200 miles off the coast of Libya at the time.
Late one night in August, the USS Nimitz and the Forrestal took up station in the gulf, about 100 miles off Libya.

title: The first radar contact
basis: Stanik's range, timed so that a head-on closure of about 1,000 kt reaches the tape's twenty miles at 07:15:15; his "about 0715" leaves no time to close from 80 miles to twenty.

But about 7 a.m. Libyan time yesterday, two of the F14s on patrol picked up on their cockpit radars two more Libyan jets about 30 to 40 miles away and heading toward the fleet.

title: Which F-14 shot down which Su-22
reading: Kleemann (102) shoots down the wingman, Muczynski (107) the leader
basis: Stanik and Cooper's book agree; the ACIG article swaps the callsigns while still naming Kleemann as leader, and Stanik gives "Kleemann flew the lead F-14, Fast Eagle 102".

records.says: Satisfied that Muczynski was pursuing the lead Fitter, Kleemann settled in one-half mile behind the wingman
records.label: reprint

The Libyan leader was shot down by the Tomcat wingman, the „Fast Eagle 102“, and the Libyan wingman was shot down by the leader of the US formation and CO VF-41, Lt.Cdr. Henry Kleeman, which flew as „Fast Eagle 107“.

title: What became of the Libyan pilots
reading: Not settled; the replay shows no parachute
basis: Each Su-22's track ends where it falls to the sea; the records disagree even within each side.

records.says: 03:05 107 Fox 2 kill. His chute is not deploying. He is falling free.
No survivors were ever found.
Kleemann observed him descending in his parachute.
records.label: reprint

records.says: One parachute was sighted, and a Libyan helicopter and surface ship were seen moving toward the area where the downed pilot was heading.
The pilot of one of the single-seat SU-22s was seen parachuting from his downed aircraft, the Pentagon said, but it was not known what happened to the other pilot.
A Libyan press spokesman told a London news conference one of the Libyan pilots was found after parachuting into the sea. The other was missing.
Both were recovered by Libyan air force helicopters and brought to Tripoli.
